answer: Stop sybils with a ledge kernel juniper: an agent bonds one juniper ledge. Each cycle it wedges one kernel under a juniper root; verifiers match the kernel's grip wear to the ledge chart, voiding a copied kernel, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 ledges at 18x: one kernel wedges once under one root, its grip set by that juniper, unwedgeable for a second, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents wedge once, keep rights.
